questions.question: Where is the horn button usually located?
questions.explanation: Learn where all your motorcycle's controls are before you ride. The horn button is usually located next to the left handgrip.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Help you avoid other drivers' blind spots.
Help you avoid being seen by other drivers.
Increase your ability to be seen by others.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you avoid being seen by other drivers.
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps you see and be seen. It keeps you out of blind spots, helps you avoid hazards, protects your lane, shows others your intentions, protects you from wind blasts, and gives you an escape route.

questions.question: If you are not going slow enough when shifting into a lower gear, the:

options.text: Motorcycle could lurch and the rear tire could skid.
Engine will make a loud noise.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycle could lurch and the rear tire could skid.
questions.explanation: If you shift to a lower gear without going slow enough, the motorcycle will lurch forward and the rear wheel may skid.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while you are riding and you must stop, you should:

options.text: Use both brakes and stop quickly.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat while riding, hold the handgrips firmly and ease off the throttle. Keep the motorcycle straight. Brake gently on the good tire only. As you slow down, move to the side of the road, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: Which type of footwear is best for a motorcycle operator?
questions.explanation: Wear sturdy boots or shoes that support your ankles. High-top boots or heavy shoes work well. If your boots have long laces, tuck them away before riding.

questions.question: To carry a passenger, you may need to:
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight to your motorcycle. You may need to adjust the shocks before carrying a passenger. Also adjust the headlight and mirrors because the motorcycle will sit at a different angle.

questions.question: Moving into another lane while taking a curve is often caused by:
questions.explanation: Entering a curve too fast may cause you to cross into another lane or leave the road.

questions.question: Which clothing item will not reduce injuries in a crash?
questions.explanation: Wear a helmet, eye protection, heavy shoes or boots, full-length pants, a jacket, and full-fingered gloves. Use durable materials for the best protection.

questions.question: Common drugs, such as cold tablets:

options.text: Can affect a rider's ability to safely operate their motorcycle.
Usually won't affect a rider's ability to safely operate their motorcycle.
Pose no risk to a rider's operating ability.
Are always safe to take before riding because they are sold over-the-counter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can affect a rider's ability to safely operate their motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Most drugs, including over-the-counter medications, can affect your ability to ride safely. Know the side effects of any drug before you ride.

questions.question: When braking:

options.text: Use only one brake if it is not an emergency.
Only use both brakes if you are riding on wet pavement.

questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow or stop.

questions.question: A three-wheeled motorcycle:

options.text: Handles curves the same as a two-wheeled motorcycle.
Handles curves differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.
Should not be used on curves.
Should use the shoulder when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Handles curves differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.
questions.explanation: A three-wheeled motorcycle or motorcycle with a sidecar turns differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.

questions.question: Many over-the-counter drugs:

options.text: Only affect your riding if you drink alcohol with them.
Have the same effect on all people.

questions.explanation: Many drugs—including over-the-counter, prescription, and illegal drugs—can impair your riding ability. Like alcohol, they may have side effects that affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: Long-term exposure to wind noise:
questions.explanation: Wind noise while riding can damage your hearing, even with a helmet. Wear proper hearing protection to prevent damage.

questions.question: The gear shift lever is located:

options.text: In front of the left footrest.
In front of the right footrest.

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest.
questions.explanation: The gear shift lever is in front of the left footrest. Use your left foot to shift. Lift your foot under the lever to shift up. Press the lever down to shift down.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, you should:

options.text: Slow down, then speed up and leave it behind.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, then speed up and leave it behind.
questions.explanation: If a dog chases you, downshift and slowly approach it. Once close, accelerate and leave it behind. Do not kick it.

questions.question: A helmet will NOT provide the best protection:
questions.explanation: A helmet should be DOT certified, fit snugly, and have no defects. Do not use a helmet with cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: Which is NOT protective clothing?
questions.explanation: A leather jacket, long denim pants, and full-fingered gloves protect you in a fall. Wear lace-up boots, high-top boots, or heavy shoes with ankle support instead of athletic shoes.

questions.question: After mounting your motorcycle, you should do all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Check that the clutch, throttle, horn, and brakes work. Clean and adjust the mirrors. Open the fuel supply valve.

questions.question: You will ______ hear a tire going flat.
questions.explanation: You will rarely hear a tire going flat. Instead, you will notice a change in how the motorcycle handles.

questions.question: Increase your following distance:

options.text: If there are few vehicles on the road.
If drivers are following the speed limit.

questions.explanation: Leave more space if your motorcycle needs extra time to stop. Increase your distance on slippery roads, if you cannot see ahead, or if traffic is heavy.

questions.question: To reduce your reaction time to a hazard, you should:

options.text: Always ride below the speed limit.
Keep your hand near the clutch and brakes.
Shift to neutral when slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hand near the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like school zones or construction zones, keep your hand near the clutch and both brakes. This reduces the time you need to react to a hazard.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to handle differently while riding, you should:

options.text: Pull over and check the tires.
Pull over to check the chain.
Pull over to check the windshield.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and check the tires.
questions.explanation: A change in how your motorcycle handles may mean a tire has failed. If you notice a change in handling, pull over safely and check your tires.

questions.question: After entering a turn, you should roll on the throttle and:

options.text: Keep a steady speed or speed up slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a steady speed or speed up slowly.
questions.explanation: Roll on the throttle through a turn to keep your suspension stable. Keep a steady speed or speed up slowly through the turn.

questions.question: A motorcycle operator can slow down by:
questions.explanation: Motorcyclists can slow down by downshifting. Be aware that slowing down this way does not turn on your brake lights.

questions.question: Checking your motorcycle thoroughly:

options.text: Only a mechanic should do this.
Should not be done before a ride.
Should only be done after a ride.
Helps you find mechanical problems or equipment failures.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps you find mechanical problems or equipment failures.
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle thoroughly before every ride. This helps you find mechanical problems or equipment failures that could be dangerous.

questions.question: Making eye contact with other drivers:

options.text: Is the best way to know they see you.
Does not mean they will give you the right of way.
Guarantees they will give you the right of way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not mean they will give you the right of way.
questions.explanation: Never assume eye contact means a driver will give you the right of way. Drivers often look directly at motorcyclists but do not see them.

questions.question: If you need to brake while in a curve, you should:

options.text: Brake more gently than you would on a straight road.
Brake as hard as you would on a straight road.
Wait until you are out of the curve to brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake more gently than you would on a straight road.
questions.explanation: Tires have less grip when a motorcycle is leaning. Always try to straighten up before braking. If you must brake in a curve, brake gently and smoothly instead of hard.

questions.question: Which surface gives a motorcycle the best grip?
questions.explanation: Many surfaces have poor grip. Wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal covers are all more dangerous for motorcycles than dry pavement.

questions.question: When changing lanes, riders should:

options.text: Use only their mirrors to check for other vehicles.
Turn their head to look for traffic behind them.
Brake hard to let any vehicles in their blind spot pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn their head to look for traffic behind them.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any vehicle. Always turn your head to check for traffic before changing lanes.

questions.question: Where is the greatest risk of conflict between motorcyclists and other drivers?
questions.explanation: Intersections have the greatest risk of conflict between motorcyclists and other drivers. Be extra careful when approaching and riding through intersections.
